# PROCESS — what I did this iteration (explainability; REQUIRED)

First real optimization iteration (parent = seed baseline, val 0.500). Diagnosed ALL 25 failing
trajectories (fanned out over 4 parallel diagnosis subagents) and confirmed the grading contract
by reading the adapter + evaluation source (read-only).

## Grading contract confirmed from source (drives the edits)
- `«redacted».py` (~line 1240): after case-1 is solved, the agent's
  FINAL solution code is **replayed verbatim on hidden inputs 2 & 3** (only the input/output
  filenames are string-substituted), then each output is graded. => code that hardcodes values,
  assumes a fixed data extent, or copies a sample tab passes case 1 and fails cases 2–3. The agent
  is never told this. Biggest lever.
- `third_party/spreadsheetbench/evaluation/evaluation.py::transform_value` + `compare_cell_value`:
  numbers→round(float,2); real dates→numeric serial; datetime.time→str; numeric text→float(coerced);
  non-numeric text stays str. Then EXACT type must match. => numeric-string vs number does NOT fail
  (coerces); the real type trap is **date-as-text vs real-date** (both directions). LibreOffice
  recalcs formulas before compare → volatile/exotic funcs recalc to blank/random/error.
- `_localize_failure`: COVERAGE feedback literally counts non-empty cells in answer_position and warns
  when the extent was assumed from the truncated preview.

## Ranked issue list (clusters by leverage, biggest first)
| rank | cluster | tasks | shared root cause | tag | change class |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Overfit to visible input / assumed data extent | 38332, 5192, 51359, 450-9, 110-2 (+ contributes to 55931, 59667, 30709) | agent doesn't know its code is re-run on hidden, differently-sized inputs; hardcodes values / fixed row range / copies sample tab / assumes data ends at preview | KNOWLEDGE | missing-rule (state grading contract) |
| 2 | Formula written instead of value | 47741, 56996, 59743, 53367 | wrote a live formula (esp. when instruction says "fix the formula"); exotic/volatile funcs recalc to blank/random | KNOWLEDGE + CONFLICT (weak "prefer" rule) | strengthen rule + add WHY/failure-modes |
| 3 | Coverage under-fill (silent lookup-miss / "" branch / partial revert) | 55931, 59667, 56637 | leaves target cells blank instead of computing a value for every applicable row | BEHAVIORAL | structure (verify checklist precondition) |
| 4 | Type mismatch on dates | 50630, 51958 | real date written as text, or text-split written as datetime | KNOWLEDGE | missing-rule (verb-conditioned type rule) |
| 5 | Genuine logic misreads (not prose-fixable) | 39046, 3911, 57090, 59259, 325-44, CF_11072, 11842, 353-29, 30709 | ambiguous multi-step spec interpreted differently from GT | (mostly out of scope) | partly helped by #1/#3; see skipped |

## Changes made this iteration
| cluster | edit class | file | what & why it generalizes | protects passing? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | missing-rule (KNOWLEDGE) | prompt.md | New "YOUR CODE IS RE-RUN ON HIDDEN INPUTS" block: compute from actual data, never hardcode values/row-range, never copy a sample tab, detect real extent (preview is truncated). General fact about grading, no task specifics. | Yes — passing tasks already generalize (passed all 3 cases); this reinforces their behavior, changes nothing they do. BOUNDED. |
| 2 | NARROW rule + WHY | prompt.md | "FORMULAS ARE RE-CALCULATED, BUT SPILL / VOLATILE FUNCTIONS ARE NOT": ordinary scalar formulas (SUM/SUMIF/INDEX-MATCH/VLOOKUP/WORKDAY/SUMPRODUCT) are explicitly OK; only dynamic-array/spill (`_xlfn.*`, TEXTJOIN-over-array, FILTER/SORT/UNIQUE/SEQUENCE) and volatile (RANDBETWEEN/NOW/TODAY) must be computed in Python. Covers "instruction says fix a formula". | Yes — CRITICAL: memory note says passing 52021, 46897, 55060, 55667, 58109 write ordinary formula strings that recalc fine; a GLOBAL literals ban would regress them. This rule is NARROW (ordinary funcs stay allowed), so it does not touch them. BOUNDED. |
| 3 | structure (BEHAVIORAL) | task_template.md | Rewrote verify step 3 into a mandatory pre-finish checklist: value+type of each cell (must be concrete, not a formula string), non-empty COUNT vs range size (fill every applicable cell), no cell outside range touched. Makes coverage/value a precondition of finishing, not advice. | Yes — adds checks a passing output already satisfies; doesn't change computed content. Conditioned on "when the instruction fills a column/block" so it won't force filling GT-blank cells or over-fill Sheet-level max-ranges. BOUNDED. |
| 4 | missing-rule (KNOWLEDGE) | prompt.md | "MATCH THE EXPECTED DATA TYPE": convert/parse/standardise→real date/number; split/extract/copy text→keep string; numeric answers as real numbers; don't leave cells blank on failed lookup. Verb-conditioned so it narrows rather than broadens. | Mostly — reinforces correct type on passing date tasks. Residual risk: a passing task with an ambiguous verb; mitigated by verb-conditioning + numeric-string coercion means only dates are actually at stake. BOUNDED (with caveat). |

## Verify-the-fix (trace → what the edit changes)
- 38332 (hardcoded `ws["D{r}"]=1`, passed case1 only): re-run block "never hardcode the answer values … derive every value from the data" → agent computes the count per unique value from column A, generalizing to cases 2–3.
- 51359 (hardcoded rows 3–14, passed case1 only): "never restrict a loop to a hardcoded row range … detect the real extent" → agent finds the actual 1/0 block extent, so hidden inputs with different heights score.
- 450-9 (copied "Wanted Results" tab): "Never copy a demonstration sheet … reproduce the LOGIC" → agent implements grouping instead of copying a tab absent/different on hidden inputs.
- 110-2 (filled 9/39, collapsed to 2 rows): "preview shows only the FIRST few rows — never assume the data ends where the preview stops" + verify COUNT check → agent fills the true extent.
- 47741 (`_xlfn.TEXTJOIN`+WORKDAY over an array, recalced blank): NARROW formula rule names exactly this spill case (`_xlfn.*`, TEXTJOIN/WORKDAY over an array) → agent computes the date-range string in Python and writes the literal. This is the cleanest win in the formula cluster.
- 56996 (INDEX/MATCH over a RANDBETWEEN source): volatile clause "cached values read from cells holding them are equally unreliable; recompute from the underlying data" → steers away from the live answer; source is fully volatile so this stays hard (noted).
- 53367 / 59743: reclassified — SUMPRODUCT (53367) and IF (59743) are ORDINARY funcs, so the narrow formula rule (correctly) does NOT force literals; their real failure is logic/operand semantics, out of prompt scope. Not claimed as formula-cluster fixes.
- 50630 (wrote datetime for a split-out date substring; GT is str): type rule "SPLIT/EXTRACT/COPY text → keep it as text" → agent writes the string, matching GT (its sibling text column already passed as str).
- 51958 (wrote "09/08/21…" as str; GT datetime): type rule "CONVERT/STANDARDISE into a date → write a REAL datetime" → agent writes a real date (serial), matching GT.
- 55931 / 59667 (left unmatched/blank cells): "Do not leave a target cell blank because a lookup failed" + verify COUNT check → agent computes a value for every applicable row.

## Process & features used
- Subagents: 4 parallel `general-purpose` diagnosis subagents, one per group of ~6 failing trajectories,
  each returning per-task root cause + cluster label. Then edits authored serially and merged into this
  one candidate (edits are small and non-conflicting; no worktrees needed).
- Prior iterations: none — this is the first iteration after the seed baseline (RUNMAP/LEDGER empty).
- Confirmed contract by reading (read-only) adapter.py + evaluation.py; did NOT edit any infra/scorer.

## Good things to PRESERVE
- The "code is re-run on hidden inputs → compute, never hardcode" knowledge is the single highest-value
  rule for this benchmark; do not weaken or delete it.
- The NARROW formula rule: ordinary scalar formulas stay allowed (they recalc fine and passing tasks 52021/46897/55060/55667/58109 rely on this); ONLY spill/dynamic-array/volatile funcs → Python literals. Do NOT turn this into a global formula ban — that regresses those 5.
- The verify-step checklist as a precondition of finishing (value+type, coverage count, in-range).

## Deliberately skipped (and why)
- Genuine logic-misread tasks (39046, 3911, 57090, 59259, 325-44, CF_11072, 11842, 353-29) — these are
  the agent interpreting an ambiguous multi-step spec differently from GT, not a knowledge/format gap
  prose can close without hardcoding the task's answer (which would overfit and fail the held-out gate).
  Several (11842, 353-29, 325-44) also had a full/near-full coverage but wrong values; #1 and #3 give
  them a better shot (generalize + fill every cell) but the core interpretation is out of prompt scope.
- 57232 (mixed int/float/str of copied lookup values) — the per-cell GT type is inconsistent and not
  derivable from the instruction; no safe general rule. Left to the type rule's general nudge only.
- No environment fault found: every rollout produced an output file and verified by re-read; no
  permission/timeout/gateway errors in the traces.
